title: Class-AB output stage (Monticelli)
description: A push-pull class-AB output stage with Monticelli floating-battery bias. The NMOS pull-down and PMOS pull-up output devices carry a quiescent current $I_q$ set by a floating voltage source between their gates. That battery defines a translinear loop: the sum of the two output devices' gate-source voltages equals the battery voltage, which fixes the quiescent current and lets it be small (low static power) while still turning fully on under drive. The consistency check is the translinear-loop equation as an equality rule with tolerance: $V_{GS,n} + |V_{GS,p}|$ must equal $V_{bat}$ at the chosen quiescent point. The swing rows give the rail-to-rail output range set by the two saturation voltages. Raising $I_q$ lowers crossover distortion but wastes static power — the class-AB quiescent/efficiency trade. On the demo NMOS table both output devices size against the same data, so the PMOS sign param stays at +1.

params.name: V_out
params.note: quiescent output DC level; sets each output device's vds

params.name: I_q
params.note: class-AB quiescent current: higher I_q lowers crossover distortion but wastes static power

params.name: V_bat
params.note: floating-battery voltage the bias network sets; the translinear loop forces Vgs_n + |Vgs_p| = V_bat at quiescent — retune to the reported vgs sum

params.name: gm_id_n
params.note: NMOS output-device inversion (low gm/ID for current drive)

params.name: p_sign
params.note: vds sign of the PMOS device table: +1 for the N-style demo axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis

doc.title: NMOS pull-down output device
doc.description: The NMOS output device at the quiescent current; its vds is the output DC level. Its vgs is one half of the translinear-loop sum.

doc.title: PMOS pull-up output device
doc.description: The PMOS output device at the quiescent current; its vds magnitude is the supply minus the output DC. Its vgs is the other half of the translinear-loop sum.

params.name: vx
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention

rows.name: vgs_sum
rows.note: the translinear-loop sum: the floating battery must supply this to bias both devices at I_q

rows.name: gm_out
rows.note: push-pull transconductance at quiescent (both devices contribute)

rows.name: swing_hi
rows.note: highest output the PMOS can pull up to while saturated

rows.name: swing_lo
rows.note: lowest output the NMOS can pull down to while saturated

rows.name: swing
rows.note: peak-to-peak output swing between the two saturation limits

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: the resistance this output stage presents at its output — both devices' output conductances in parallel, since at quiescent they conduct together. The gain assumes a capacitive load, so nothing here models a resistive one; this row is what a composing parent checks its own loading against

rules.note: translinear-loop consistency: the floating-battery voltage must equal Vgs_n + |Vgs_p| at the quiescent current, or the design biases at a different I_q than intended — retune V_bat to the reported vgs_sum
